title: Strengthening India’s Nuclear Energy Ecosystem
description: This editorial is based on “India turns to nuclear power as Gulf risks rise” published in The Economic Times on 09/06/2026. The article states that to meet its 100 GW target by 2047, India is leveraging the SHANTI Act and new reactor milestones, but must overcome high costs, land issues, and resource gaps to ensure energy security. For Prelims: Nuclear Energy, SHANTI Act, 2025, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), Stage II PFBR Criticality, Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR), Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), SWIFT, Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project, Digital Twin. For Mains: Reforms in India's nuclear energy framework, hurdles in India’s nuclear energy modernisation and steps needed for long-term scalability of the nuclear energy ecosystem. Amid rising geopolitical risks in the Gulf and a persistent reliance on coal, India is renewing its focus on nuclear energy as a stable, domestic baseload source, leveraging indigenous technological milestones and policy reforms to diversify its energy mix and reduce import vulnerability. India’s shift toward a nuclear-led energy strategy, driven by the SHANTI Act, 2025, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and Stage II PFBR criticality, represents a critical move to ensure energy Aatmanirbharta.
